title: Not All Bits Are Equal: How Model Scale Changes Memory-Optimal Reasoning
venue_full: The Fourteenth International Conference on Learning Representations

problem_statement.en: Reasoning models generate significantly more tokens than non-reasoning models, causing the KV cache to become a dominant memory bottleneck that renders scale-agnostic memory optimization strategies ineffective.
problem_statement.zh: 推理模型（reasoning model）生成的 token 數量遠多於非推理模型，使 KV cache 成為主導性記憶體瓶頸，令與規模無關的記憶體最佳化策略失效。

key_innovation.en: A scale-dependent memory allocation framework for reasoning models that determines the optimal trade-off between model weight precision, effective model size, and KV cache compression (eviction vs. quantization) based on the model's effective size.
key_innovation.zh: 一個針對推理模型的規模相關記憶體分配框架，根據模型的有效規模，在模型權重精度、有效模型大小與 KV cache 壓縮方式（eviction 對比 quantization）之間確定最優取捨。

evaluation_and_results.baselines_compared: vLLM, GPTQ, AWQ, FP8, R-KV, StreamingLLM, HQQ

key_improvements.en: Identified a scale-dependent threshold (8-bit 4B effective size) for memory-optimal strategies; demonstrated that KV cache compression (eviction/quantization) consistently advances the Pareto frontier.
key_improvements.zh: 識別出記憶體最優策略的規模相關閾值（8-bit、4B 有效規模）；並驗證 KV cache 壓縮（eviction/quantization）能穩定推進 Pareto 前沿。

workload_and_traffic.ai_task: LLM Serving, Reasoning, Mathematical Reasoning, Code Generation, Knowledge-intensive Reasoning
workload_and_traffic.traffic_pattern: Serial Scaling, Parallel Scaling, Majority Voting
